answer: Use a sequential proof-of-work puzzle bound to each key, renewed every epoch. A registrant hashes its public key plus the previous block hash through a memory-hard function that cannot be parallelized, taking about six hours on one core. Validators verify the result in milliseconds and drop identities whose proof lapses. A forger of a thousand keys must rent a thousand cores continuously, about two dollars daily each, so the knoll of fakes never grows into a gale, and each pulse of renewal taxes them again.
